name: proximal_phrase_anchors_to_conversation_now
description: v15.9 adds an explicit rule: when the operator uses a proximal-time phrase ('just got back', 'just attended', 'recently', 'we just X', 'today I did X') for their own personal experience, event_time MUST anchor to conversation_now, not to any scout-extracted date for the same event. Pairs with the temporal scout's new source_role tagging (the scout now marks each candidate's attributing role) so the encoder can also discriminate user-attributed dates from assistant-paraphrased ones.
target_behavior: For gpt4_85da3956 (Universal Studios visit, conversation_now=2023-07-15): the encoder should set event_time='2023-07-15' (conversation_now) on the Universal Studios event node, NOT '2023-06-24' (the date the prior assistant turn introduced when paraphrasing the user's 'just got back' as 'three weeks ago'). The operator never named a specific date for the visit; only the assistant did.
location_hint: ## Temporal anchoring — new subsections 'Proximal phrases anchor to conversation_now' and 'Speaker-attributed dates — user beats assistant', inserted between 'What the temporal scout gives you' and 'Cross-event temporal flow'. Plus a new Example 4 demonstrating the assistant-paraphrased-proximal-phrase pattern.
before_text:
Resolve relative phrases to ISO at encode time, using the conversation timestamp the scout exposes:

- **Resolvable**: phrase has a determinate offset from the anchor. 'today' → conversation date. 'yesterday' → -1 day. 'last Tuesday' → most recent Tuesday before anchor. '2 weeks ago' → -14 days. 'in March' → if year is unambiguous from anchor, use that. Resolve these.
- **Unresolvable**: phrase has no anchor or the offset is vague AND no catalog landmark resolves it. 'a few weeks ago' (vague + no anchor), 'before the move' (no dated move in catalog), 'around when X happened' (X undated). Leave event_time absent — don't guess.

The line: if you can name a specific day/range from the anchor + the phrase, resolve it. If you'd be inventing the day, don't.

(No subsection on proximal phrases. No subsection on speaker attribution. Scout candidate spec does not include source_role or evidence_roles.)
after_text:
### Proximal phrases anchor to conversation_now

When the operator uses a proximal-time phrase for their own experience — 'just got back from X', 'just attended X', 'just finished X', 'we recently did X', 'we just X', 'today I did X' — set event_time to the conversation date (current_date / conversation_now), NOT to any scout-extracted date for the same event.

Why: scouts collect every date phrase from the whole conversation, including dates the assistant introduced while paraphrasing the operator. For phrases the operator used about a personal experience, conversation_now is the correct anchor; any specific date the scout surfaced from elsewhere is event metadata about the event itself (e.g. the festival's run dates, a venue's opening), not the operator's report-date.

Concrete: operator says 'I just got back from the Summer Nights festival at Universal.' Scout returns candidates [conversation_date, 2023-06-24, ...]. Pick conversation_date.

### Speaker-attributed dates — user beats assistant

Read each candidate's source_role:

- source_role: 'user' — operator-attributed. Trust as the resolution authority. Use this date for event_time.
- source_role: 'assistant' AND no user-attributed candidate exists for the same event — the date is the assistant's inference. For the operator's proximal phrase, prefer conversation_now. Do NOT anchor the event to an assistant-only date.
- source_role: 'assistant' AND a different user-attributed candidate exists for the same event — the operator wins. Use the user's date.

Authority order: user-attributed date > conversation_now (for proximal operator phrases) > assistant-attributed date.

Plus a new Example 4 showing the exact gpt4_85da3956 case (operator 'just got back', assistant paraphrased 'three weeks ago', encoder anchors to conversation_now=2023-07-15).

The scout candidate spec is updated to include source_role and evidence_roles fields.
